aou_req__time__user_initializes_backend.content:
The Component User shall initialize the backends for clock domains
that require initialization before requesting time snapshots
from those domains.
aou_req__time__user_initializes_backend.title: Backend initialization by the user

aou_req__time_daemon__gptp_shm_available.content: The user shall ensure gPTP shared memory is initialized and the time_slave component is running before starting time_daemon. Starting time_daemon without an initialized shared memory region will cause shared memory access failures or reading of stale/uninitialized time data during startup.
aou_req__time_daemon__gptp_shm_available.title: gPTP Shared Memory Availability

aou_req__time_slave__hw_timestamping.content: If the user has high demands regarding the synchronization accuracy and precision, they must configure a NIC providing hardware timestamping and driver software support.
aou_req__time_slave__hw_timestamping.title: Hardware Timestamping Support

aou_req__time_slave__network_config.content: The user shall configure a network interface and ensure the interface has an assigned link-layer address and the link is operationally up (IFF_UP and IFF_RUNNING flags set) before starting time_slave.
aou_req__time_slave__network_config.title: Network Interface Configuration

aou_req__time_slave__single_instance.content: The user shall run exactly one time_slave instance only. Multiple instances are not supported and will cause failures or conflicts on the single IPC interface to the TimeDaemon.
aou_req__time_slave__single_instance.title: Single Instance per Interface

aou_req__ts_client__shm_permissions.content: The user shall configure system permissions to allow publisher write access and readers read access to shared memory segments. Incorrect permissions will cause channel creation or opening failures.
aou_req__ts_client__shm_permissions.title: Shared Memory Permissions

aou_req__ts_client__single_publisher.content: The ts_client user shall ensure that only one publisher process opens and writes to a shared memory segment to maintain data consistency. Multiple publishers writing to the same segment will cause data corruption and readers will receive invalid data.
aou_req__ts_client__single_publisher.title: Single Publisher Process

comp_req__high_res_steady_time__snapshot.content:
The Component shall provide steady high-resolution time snapshots
without requiring prior initialization.
comp_req__high_res_steady_time__snapshot.title: HighResSteadyClock always-ready snapshot

comp_req__steady_time__snapshot.content:
The Component shall provide steady time snapshots without
requiring prior initialization, and shall cause compilation failure
when initialization or availability operations are invoked on the
steady time domain.
comp_req__steady_time__snapshot.title: SteadyClock always-ready snapshot

comp_req__system_time__snapshot.content:
The Component shall provide system time snapshots without
requiring prior initialization, and shall cause compilation failure
when initialization or availability operations are invoked on the
system time domain.
comp_req__system_time__snapshot.title: SystemClock always-ready snapshot

comp_req__time__explicit_lifecycle.content:
The Component shall provide initialization, availability-check, and
availability-wait operations for clock domains that depend on external
resources, and shall cause compilation failure when those operations
are invoked on clock domains that are always ready.
comp_req__time__explicit_lifecycle.title: Explicit lifecycle for backends that need it

comp_req__time__snapshot_with_status.content:
The Component shall return a single immutable value that bundles
the timepoint with the domain's synchronization and quality
metadata, so callers observe state that cannot change after
creation and can determine time validity without a separate
status query.
comp_req__time__snapshot_with_status.title: Immutable snapshot with quality metadata

comp_req__time__supported_platforms.content:
The Component shall build and run on Linux and QNX host platforms,
providing platform-specific backends where the underlying OS APIs
differ.
comp_req__time__supported_platforms.title: Supported platforms

comp_req__time__unified_clock_facade.content:
The Component shall provide a single type-safe accessor for all supported
clock domains that prevents mixing time values from different domains by
rejecting domain-mismatched operations at compile time when accessing
time snapshots.
comp_req__time__unified_clock_facade.title: Unified clock facade across time domains

comp_req__time_daemon__error_reporting.content: The time_daemon component shall log messages via the score::mw::log interface when initialization fails (error level), shared memory access fails (error level), verification stage failures occur (warning level), or time synchronization data reception fails (error level).
comp_req__time_daemon__error_reporting.title: Error Reporting

comp_req__time_daemon__gptp_shm_receptio.content: The time_daemon component shall receive time synchronization data from time_slave component using the ts_client component for IPC abstraction.
comp_req__time_daemon__gptp_shm_receptio.title: Time Synchronization Data Reception

comp_req__time_daemon__multi_client.content: The time_daemon component shall support concurrent non-blocking read access from multiple client applications to the published time data.
comp_req__time_daemon__multi_client.title: Multi-Client Support

comp_req__time_daemon__non_blocking.content: The time_daemon component shall use a non-blocking, lock-free shared memory access path for receiving time synchronization data and providing published time data to client applications.
comp_req__time_daemon__non_blocking.title: Non-Blocking Access Path

comp_req__time_daemon__platform_support.content: The time_daemon component shall support POSIX and QNX 8.0 SDPplatforms for shared memory access and IPC communication.
comp_req__time_daemon__platform_support.title: Platform Support

comp_req__time_daemon__publish_interval.content: The time_daemon component shall publish time data to client applications at a fixed configurable interval (default: 250 milliseconds).
comp_req__time_daemon__publish_interval.title: Publish Interval

comp_req__time_daemon__published_data_co.content:
The time_daemon component shall include in published time data: the timestamp of the master clock, the corresponding timestamp of the local reference clock, the rate deviation between those two clocks, synchronization status, time jump status, and timeout status.

Also it shall include condensed raw data of the last received Sync/FollowUp pair and the last finished Pdelay measurement.
comp_req__time_daemon__published_data_co.title: Published Time Data Content

comp_req__time_daemon__shutdown.content: The time_daemon component shall stop the publishing loop and close plus release any IPC resources (e.g. shared memory mappings) when a stop signal is received.
comp_req__time_daemon__shutdown.title: Component Shutdown

comp_req__time_daemon__startup.content: On startup the time_daemon component shall determine its configuration, initialize the configured time synchronization data receiver, time data verification pipeline (synchronization validation, timeout detection, time jump detection), and IPC publisher. If initialization of any of those units fails, the time_daemon shall retry to initialize the respective unit. Overall initialization shall fail if not completed within 20 seconds and shall end the time_slave process.
comp_req__time_daemon__startup.title: Component Initialization

comp_req__time_daemon__sync_debounce.content: The time_daemon component shall not report time jumps during the configured time span (default: 5 seconds) after initial synchronization to avoid spuriously detected time jumps during startup.
comp_req__time_daemon__sync_debounce.title: Synchronization State Stabilization

comp_req__time_daemon__sync_validation.content: The time_daemon component shall validate synchronization status based on received time synchronization data.
comp_req__time_daemon__sync_validation.title: Synchronization Status Validation

comp_req__time_daemon__time_data_publish.content: The time_daemon component shall publish the verified time synchronization data to the time component linked as a library into client applications.
comp_req__time_daemon__time_data_publish.title: Time Data Publishing

comp_req__time_daemon__time_jump_detecti.content: The time_daemon component shall detect time jumps when the master clock timestamp of a gPTP time sync data update differs from the expected value by more than the configured time span (default: 500 microseconds). Both forward and backward time jumps shall be detected.
comp_req__time_daemon__time_jump_detecti.title: Time Jump Detection

comp_req__time_daemon__time_jump_reactio.content: The time_daemon component shall continue publishing time data with time jump status set when time jump is detected.
comp_req__time_daemon__time_jump_reactio.title: Time Jump Error Reaction

comp_req__time_daemon__time_jump_recover.content: The time_daemon component shall clear time jump condition after receiving 2 consecutive valid gPTP frames without time jump.
comp_req__time_daemon__time_jump_recover.title: Time Jump Recovery

comp_req__time_daemon__time_point_qualif.content: The time_daemon component shall determine the time point qualifier (quality indicator) of the published time data from the outcome of the synchronization, time jump and timeout verification checks.
comp_req__time_daemon__time_point_qualif.title: Time Point Qualifier Production

comp_req__time_daemon__timeout_detection.content: The time_daemon component shall detect timeout condition when no new time synchronization data is received within the configured time span (default: 3.3 seconds).
comp_req__time_daemon__timeout_detection.title: Timeout Detection

comp_req__time_daemon__timeout_reaction.content: The time_daemon component shall continue publishing time data with timeout status set when the timeout detection period elapses without receiving new gPTP data.
comp_req__time_daemon__timeout_reaction.title: Timeout Error Reaction

comp_req__time_slave__configuration.content:
The time_slave component shall try to read its configuration from a file. The file location is defined in this order:
 1. Specified by command line argument `--config <filepath>`,
 2. specified by environment variable `TIMESLAVE_CONFIG`,
 3. the default path `./etc/time_slave_config.json`.

If the defined file is not present or its parsing fails (due to malformed content), a warning shall be generated and predefined default values shall be used for the configuration items.
Likewise, if certain configuration items are missing in the file, their predefined default values shall be used.
comp_req__time_slave__configuration.title: Component Configuration

comp_req__time_slave__diagnostics.content: The time_slave component shall provide optional runtime instrumentation to record gPTP synchronization events (peer delay completion, offset thresholds, time leaps) to a CSV file for debugging and diagnostics when enabled via the GptpEngineOptions diagnostics configuration parameter.
comp_req__time_slave__diagnostics.title: Synchronization Diagnostics

comp_req__time_slave__domain_filtering.content: According to IEEE 802.1AS, the time_slave component shall only process received gPTP Sync and FollowUp messages matching the configured domain number (0-127 per IEEE 802.1AS). The time_slave component shall ignore the domain number contained in received gPTP Pdelay messages. It shall set the domain number to 0 in sent gPTP Pdelay messages (see IEEE 802.1AS-2011, section 8.1 and IEEE 802.1AS-2020, section 11.1.2, 2nd paragraph).
comp_req__time_slave__domain_filtering.title: Domain Number Filtering

comp_req__time_slave__error_reporting.content: The time_slave component shall log messages via the score::mw::log interface when initialization fails (error level), network operations fail (error level), protocol errors occur (error level), or hardware timestamping is unavailable (warning level).
comp_req__time_slave__error_reporting.title: Error Reporting

comp_req__time_slave__ethernet_address.content: The time_slave component shall receive the IEEE 802.1AS messages Sync, Follow_Up, PdelayReq, Pdelay_Resp, and Pdelay_Resp_Follow_Up sent to the Ethernet address specified in the IEEE 801.1AS standard. It shall send outgoing Pdelay messages (Pdelay_Req, Pdelay_Resp, and Pdelay_Resp_Follow_Up) to the same address.
comp_req__time_slave__ethernet_address.title: Ethernet address usage

comp_req__time_slave__followup_processin.content: The time_slave component shall process IEEE 802.1AS Follow_Up messages, match them to the corresponding Sync message by sequence ID, and extract the precise origin timestamp.
comp_req__time_slave__followup_processin.title: Follow_Up Message Processing

comp_req__time_slave__offset_calculation.content: The time_slave component shall compute the clock offset as the difference between the local receive timestamp and the Grand Master origin timestamp, accounting for the correction fields from both the Sync and Follow_Up messages per IEEE 802.1AS.
comp_req__time_slave__offset_calculation.title: Offset Calculation

comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_computation.content: The time_slave component shall compute network propagation delay from PDelayResp and PDelayRespFollowUp timestamps using the IEEE 802.1AS propagation delay formula: ((t4 - t1) - (t3 - t2)) / 2, where t2 is the requestReceiptTimestamp and t3 is the responseOriginTimestamp each corrected by the correctionField of the corresponding PdelayResp or PdelayRespFollowUp message.
comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_computation.title: Peer Delay Computation

comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_req.content: After the configured initial warmup delay (default: 2000 milliseconds), the time_slave component shall periodically transmit IEEE 802.1AS PDelayReq messages at the configured interval (default: 1000 milliseconds) and record the transmit timestamp.
comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_req.title: PDelayReq Transmission

comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_req_respons.content: The time_slave component shall receive IEEE 802.1AS PDelayReq messages from peer nodes, record the receive timestamp, and respond with PDelayResp and PDelayRespFollowUp messages containing the requestReceiptTimestamp and responseOriginTimestamp per IEEE 802.1AS peer delay mechanism.
comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_req_respons.title: PDelayReq Response

comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_resp_fu_rx.content: The time_slave component shall receive IEEE 802.1AS PDelayRespFollowUp messages, match them to the corresponding PDelayResp message by sequence ID, and extract the responseOriginTimestamp.
comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_resp_fu_rx.title: PDelayRespFollowUp Message Reception

comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_resp_recept.content: The time_slave component shall receive IEEE 802.1AS PDelayResp messages in response to transmitted PDelayReq messages and extract the requestReceiptTimestamp from the message.
comp_req__time_slave__pdelay_resp_recept.title: PDelayResp Message Reception

comp_req__time_slave__phc_frequency.content: The time_slave component shall slew-adjust the PTP hardware clock frequency based on the neighbor rate ratio computed from consecutive Sync/Follow_Up pairs with positive time intervals per IEEE 802.1AS Clause 11.4.1.
comp_req__time_slave__phc_frequency.title: PHC Frequency Adjustment

comp_req__time_slave__phc_offset.content: The time_slave component shall step-adjust the PTP hardware clock (PHC - the network interface hardware clock used for timestamping per IEEE 1588/802.1AS) offset when the absolute value of the computed offset exceeds the configured step threshold (configurable, default 1 second).
comp_req__time_slave__phc_offset.title: PHC Offset Adjustment

comp_req__time_slave__platform_support.content: The time_slave component shall support POSIX and QNX 8.0 SDP platforms for Ethernet frame transmission/reception with hardware timestamping and PTP hardware clock control.
comp_req__time_slave__platform_support.title: Platform Support

comp_req__time_slave__shutdown.content: On receiving a stop signal the time_slave component shall stop message processing threads, close network sockets, and release IPC resources.
comp_req__time_slave__shutdown.title: Component Shutdown

comp_req__time_slave__startup.content: On startup the time_slave component shall determine its configuration, initialize the gPTP engine and IPC publisher, bind to the configured network interface, and attempt to enable hardware timestamping on the network interface during initialization. Any (unrecoverable) error shall terminate the startup procedure and end the time_slave process.
comp_req__time_slave__startup.title: Component Startup

comp_req__time_slave__sync_publishing.content: The time_slave component shall publish synchronized time data (PTP assumed time, offset correction, rate deviation, peer delay, status flags) via the ts_client IPC interface at a fixed interval of 50 milliseconds to provide consistent read latency for VehicleTime clients.
comp_req__time_slave__sync_publishing.title: Time Sync Data Publishing

comp_req__time_slave__sync_reception.content: The time_slave component shall receive IEEE 802.1AS Sync messages from the network Grand Master via the IEEE 802.1AS-specified Ethernet address and determine the receive timestamp using hardware timestamping when available, otherwise using software timestamping as a fallback.
comp_req__time_slave__sync_reception.title: Sync Message Reception

comp_req__ts_client__cache_optimization.content: The ts_client component shall optimize shared memory layout to prevent cache contention between concurrent writer and reader processes.
comp_req__ts_client__cache_optimization.title: Cache-Optimized Memory Layout

comp_req__ts_client__data_validity.content: The ts_client Receiver shall indicate whether the shared memory channel is obviously corrupted.
comp_req__ts_client__data_validity.title: Data Validity Indication

comp_req__ts_client__pdelay_data.content: The ts_client component shall exchange gPTP Peer Delay (PDelay) message metadata containing request origin timestamp, request receipt timestamp, response origin timestamp, response receipt timestamp, path delay measurement, request port number, response port number, request clock identity, response clock identity, reference global timestamp, and reference local timestamp.
comp_req__ts_client__pdelay_data.title: PDelay Message Metadata Exchange

comp_req__ts_client__platform_support.content: The ts_client component shall support POSIX and QNX 8.0 SDP platforms for shared memory operations and inter-process communication.
comp_req__ts_client__platform_support.title: Platform Support

comp_req__ts_client__publisher_creates.content: The ts_client Publisher shall create shared memory channels that Receivers subsequently open.
comp_req__ts_client__publisher_creates.title: Publisher Creates Channels

comp_req__ts_client__receiver_multi_read.content: The ts_client Receiver shall support multiple concurrent readers accessing shared memory channels in read-only mode.
comp_req__ts_client__receiver_multi_read.title: Receiver Multi-Reader Semantics

comp_req__ts_client__seqlock_protocol.content: The ts_client component shall implement non-blocking synchronization between writer and readers and ensure readers can detect concurrent writes.
comp_req__ts_client__seqlock_protocol.title: Lock-Free Synchronization

comp_req__ts_client__shared_memory_mgmt.content: The ts_client component shall provide operations to create, open, and close shared memory channels for gPTP data exchange between time_slave and time_daemon.
comp_req__ts_client__shared_memory_mgmt.title: Shared Memory Channel Management

comp_req__ts_client__shm_validation.content: The ts_client component shall validate shared memory region integrity on Open operations and reject regions that fail validation.
comp_req__ts_client__shm_validation.title: Shared Memory Region Validation

comp_req__ts_client__sync_fup_data.content: The ts_client component shall exchange gPTP Sync and FollowUp message metadata containing precise origin timestamp, reference global timestamp, reference local timestamp, sync ingress timestamp, correction field, sequence identifier, path delay, port number, and clock identity.
comp_req__ts_client__sync_fup_data.title: Sync/FollowUp Message Metadata Exchange

comp_req__ts_client__sync_status_data.content: The ts_client component shall exchange gPTP synchronization status information containing synchronized state and timeout condition.
comp_req__ts_client__sync_status_data.title: gPTP Synchronization Status Exchange

comp_req__ts_client__time_correlation_da.content: The ts_client component shall exchange time correlation data containing synchronized PTP assumed time, local system time reference, and clock rate deviation.
comp_req__ts_client__time_correlation_da.title: Time Correlation Data Exchange

comp_req__vehicle_time__lifecycle.content:
The Component shall delegate initialization and
availability checks to the backend and shall report backend
init failure and availability-wait timeouts to the caller without
blocking indefinitely.
comp_req__vehicle_time__lifecycle.title: VehicleClock lifecycle operations

comp_req__vehicle_time__snapshot.content:
The Component shall read the vehicle time timepoint and its status
atomically from the backend within a single backend operation, so
downstream callers observe consistent time and status values.
comp_req__vehicle_time__snapshot.title: VehicleClock returns snapshot with status

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.
